newsitem.title: INDIA: India Morgan Stanley says studying SEBI order.
newsitem.headline: India Morgan Stanley says studying SEBI order.

text.p: Morgan Stanley Asset Management India Pvt Ltd on Monday said it was studying an order received from India's capital market regulator about violations of mutual fund regulations.
The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) on Monday said it slapped a 200,000 rupees ($5,587) penalty on Morgan Stanley Asset Management for violating Indian mutual fund regulations.
"These violations were of the investment norms prescribed by SEBI in the mutual fund regulations," SEBI said in a statement.

"Morgan Stanley treats compliance matters with the utmost seriousness and we are currently studying the content of the adjudication order carefully in order to consider the options available to us," a spokesperson of the Indian subsidiary of the US-based investment bank told Reuters.
Morgan Stanley operates a close-ended mutual fund which has been quoted below par.
SEBI said the violations included undertaking activity akin to an asset management company for clients other than the Morgan Stanley Mutual Fund without prior approval of SEBI, the watchdog said.
The statement said Morgan Stanley also exceeded the five percent investment ceiling norm in company stocks and failure to deliver securities sold in the market.

"Accordingly, the adjudicating officer has after considering (Morgan Stanley's) replies (to the charges), other submissions made by the fund and personal hearing has come to the conclusion that violations did take place..."

SEBI had appointed an adjudicating officer to look into the fund's operations following findings of an inspection carried out by independent auditors into its affairs and on the basis of the fund's annual report for 1995/96 (April-March).
